summary: The study investigates the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of TiO2 and ZrO2 using heteroleptic guanidinate precursors [Ti(NEtMe)3(guan-NEtMe)] and [Zr(NEtMe)3(guan-NEtMe)] with water or ozone as oxygen sources. The processes exhibit self-limiting growth at 275°C, with high growth rates for ZrO2. The films are smooth and have high purity when ozone is used as the oxygen source. The study compares these processes with previous studies on guanidinate precursors.
evidence: In this study the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of TiO2 and ZrO2 using two heteroleptic amido-guanidinate precursors, [Ti(NEtMe)3(guan-NEtMe)] and [Zr(NEtMe)3(guan-NEtMe)], together with water or ozone as oxygen sources, are investigated. All processes exhibit self-limiting growth at a deposition temperature of 275°C. The zirconium precursor especially gives high growth rates (0.8/1.0 Å per cycle with H2O/O3). The films are also relatively smooth, as determined by atomic force microscopy (AFM). The composition of the films is examined using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and time of flight elastic recoil detection analysis (TOF-ERDA). When using ozone as the oxygen source the films present very high purity.
